text: Suddenly. I was paddling out and suddenly the wind changed.
Notice. When I came up, I did not notice the second wave.
Snap. I heard the board snap under my feet.
Shout. He started to shout from the beach.
Panic. Do not panic. Stay with your board.
Whitewater. I was under the whitewater for twenty seconds.
Shallow. It is very shallow near the sandbank.
Hold your breath. The only thing you can do is hold your breath and wait.
I was paddling out when I saw it.
What were you doing when it happened?
While I was waiting, the wind changed.
You're late. What happened out there?
I was paddling out and suddenly a big set came from nowhere.
Did you get through it?
No. I was holding my breath under the first wave when the second one hit me.
Were you in the whitewater the whole time?
About twenty seconds. When I came up, I noticed my board was gone.
Did it snap?
In two pieces. I didn't panic though. It was shallow near the sandbank, so I walked in.
And nobody saw any of it?
My brother was watching from the beach. He shouted something, but I was still coughing and I didn't hear him.
I was paddling out when it happened.
While I was waiting, my board snapped.
Sorry, mate. I wasn't looking.
Suddenly everybody on the beach started shouting.

Good morning, everyone. One quick word before you go in. At about seven this morning a young surfer was paddling out on the north side when the sand moved under him and the rip took him eighty meters down the beach. He did the right thing. He was not panicking, he was not swimming against the water, he was just holding on to his board and waving one arm. We had him out in four minutes. So, two things for today. Do not surf the north corner on a falling tide, and if something goes wrong out there, stay with your board and shout.

The funny part is that I was having the best session of the month. Small, clean, nobody out. I was riding a wave into the shallow part, thinking about breakfast, honestly, when I heard this crack under my feet. I looked down and the board was in two pieces. And I was not even doing anything special. No air, no big turn, nothing. I was standing there going straight. My mate was filming from the beach and he got all of it, so now the whole club has seen me fall off a broken board in water up to my knees. He has not stopped sending it to people since Tuesday.
